insights.headline: IGST edge on bank gold imports ends as LBMA delegates project $5,013 gold in 12 months
insights.summary: India withdrew the upfront IGST exemption on bullion imports by banks and nominated agencies, confirming the 3% levy since April 1. Globally, LBMA conference delegates projected gold near $5,013/oz and silver near $97.40 within 12 months, after September's 8.5% drop — gold's worst month of 2026 — even as gold ETFs drew a record $31B in Q3. COMEX gold closed the week up 1.39% with spot near $4,195; the RBI defends the rupee with a dollar window for oil firms from Oct 12. US September CPI lands October 14.
points: IGST parity: banks now pay 3% IGST upfront on bullion imports, same as other routes, since April 1 (Revenue Secretary).
LBMA poll: delegates project gold $5,013/oz and silver $97.40/oz in 12 months (~19.5% and ~60% upside); Metals Focus sees a $5,330 gold average in 2027.
Weekly rebound: COMEX gold +1.39% and silver +1.15% on the week, spot gold near $4,195; silver's 2.8% Friday bounce clashes with fading solar demand.
Institutional bid: gold ETFs drew $31B in Q3, holdings at a record 4,256t (WGC); China added gold for a 23rd straight month, Poland nears its 700t target.
RBI's rupee defence: dollar window for state oil firms from Oct 12; forex reserves fell $12.95B to $734.61B in the week ended Oct 2.

trending.title: The tax edge on bank gold imports is gone
trending.summary: Banks and nominated agencies have paid 3% IGST on bullion imports since April 1 — the 2017 exemption is over, levelling the field with routes like the IIBX and adding a cost layer to bank shipments.

trending.title: Industry bets big: $5,013 gold in 12 months
trending.summary: LBMA delegates see ~19.5% upside for gold and ~60% for silver over the next year, backed by record $31B Q3 ETF inflows and relentless central-bank buying — even after September's 8.5% sell-off.

trending.title: Silver's bounce masks a fading industrial engine
trending.summary: Silver settled near $61 on Friday but sits 50% below its January peak; solar silver demand seen falling 186.6 to 151 Moz in 2026, with SHFE silver down three weeks straight.

trending.title: RBI's rupee defence goes into overdrive
trending.summary: A dollar window for oil firms from Oct 12 and tighter hedging rules fight to steady the rupee — a direct cost driver for bullion imports; reserves fell $12.95B in a week.

trending.title: Festive season, delayed — and price-sensitive
trending.summary: Jewellers report Q2 growth cooling ahead of a delayed festive season; shoppers await price stability, and in Lucknow record silver prices threaten the famed bridal nagra craft.

items.title: India ends IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imports by banks
items.summary: The government has withdrawn the upfront IGST exemption banks and nominated agencies enjoyed on bullion imports since 2017. Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava says banks have paid the 3% IGST since April 1, 2026; the GST Council was informed on October 8. Bank-channel imports now sit on par with routes like the India International Bullion Exchange, removing a tax edge that favoured one channel.

items.title: LBMA conference delegates project gold at $5,013/oz and silver at $97.40 within 12 months
items.summary: LBMA conference delegates in Sorrento projected gold near $5,013/oz and silver near $97.40/oz within about 12 months — roughly 19.5% and 60% above last week's closes, Discovery Alert reports. The call followed September's 8.5% drop, gold's worst month of 2026, even as gold ETFs drew a record $31B in Q3. The PBoC bought gold for a 23rd straight month.

items.title: Gold's Rebound Meets a Wall of Rate Expectations
items.summary: Spot gold finished Friday at $4,196.07/oz (+1.5%) on bargain hunting, softer oil, a weaker dollar and easing yields, per Reuters. Rate bets cap the rebound: 18% for October, 82% for December. StoneX sees a $4,000 floor; Bybit warns of a more aggressive Fed. WGC: gold ETFs drew $10B (67t) in September to a record 4,256t; China added 740,000 oz, a 23rd straight month. US CPI Oct 14.

items.title: Silver's 2.8% Bounce Masks a Deeper Reckoning: Solar Demand Is Fading and London's Vaults Are Overflowing
items.summary: Silver rose 2.8% Friday to $61.11/oz as yields retreated, but sits ~50% below its $121.78 52-week high. Industry is sputtering: silver use in electronics incl. solar at 422.9 Moz in 2026 vs 449.5 Moz in 2025; PV demand shrinks 186.6 to 151.0 Moz. Deutsche Bank sees China solar use down ~33% and a surplus as early as 2027. London vaults held 914+ Moz at end-August; stock up ~70% since Oct 2025.

items.title: RBI opens dollar window for oil firms from Oct 12, tightens forex hedging rules
items.summary: The RBI will meet the daily dollar needs of Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL through designated banks from October 12, shifting a major source of dollar demand off the spot market as the rupee hovers near record lows. It also barred rebooking of cancelled forex derivative contracts, cut the no-proof position limit to $5 million, and imposed a 20% cash reserve on rupee-linked derivatives above $2 million.

items.title: UK overtakes China as biggest source of gold ETF inflows in 2026: What is driving the surge?
items.summary: UK-listed gold ETFs drew $9.5bn in net inflows in Jan–Sep 2026, overtaking China's $9.46bn as the largest country-level source of gold ETF demand, World Gold Council data shows. The UK's $7.5bn Q3 haul — its strongest quarter on record — helped Europe beat North America for the quarter. The WGC cites UK fiscal worries, a weak pound and a high gilt term premium as possible drivers.

items.title: Metals broadly rise overnight as COMEX gold and silver post weekly gains
items.summary: COMEX gold rose 1.52% overnight and closed the week up 1.39%, while COMEX silver gained 2.84% overnight and 1.15% on the week, Shanghai Metals Market's October 10 recap says. SHFE gold edged up 0.4% while SHFE silver fell a third straight week, down 1.41%. The dollar index held at 102.23; US September CPI and PPI land next week.

items.title: Will gold prices fall further? The forces pulling both ways
items.summary: Spot gold stood near $4,195 on October 10, down about 5% in 2026 and roughly 26% from January's $5,595 peak, with Indian prices down nearly 23%. The drags: US 10-year near 5.27%, a dollar index up over 3% this year, rate-hike fears, oil-linked inflation worries and profit-taking. The bull case: central-bank buying near 700 tonnes in 2026 (Mirae Asset MF) plus India's festive and wedding demand.

items.title: Gold jewellers brace for Q3 after growth cools in Q2
items.summary: Gold retailers posted strong but moderating September-quarter growth as the festive and wedding season slipped into the December quarter, an Equirus analyst said. Titan's jewellery-led revenue grew 25% in Q2 FY27 versus 40%+ in the prior three quarters; Kalyan Jewellers grew over 26%. With gold still above Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams, shoppers are waiting for price stability before buying.

items.title: Gold buying picks up after price correction, but shoppers prioritise affordability
items.summary: Indian gold retailers report customer footfall picking up after the price correction from the highs, but shoppers are prioritising affordability and staying within budgets, ET Bureau reports.

items.title: High silver prices threaten Lucknow's famed bridal nagra craft
items.summary: Al Jazeera profiles Lucknow's silver nagra bridal-shoe makers, a craft collapsing as Indian silver hit about ₹250,000/kg — over three times 2023 levels. Pairs that once sold for ₹12,000 now cost ₹60,000–75,000, pricing out brides, and most of the ~30 craftsmen have quit. India more than doubled effective gold/silver import taxes in May; silver imports then plunged 87%.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in week ended Oct 2
items.summary: India's forex reserves fell $12.95bn to $734.61bn in the week ended October 2, RBI data released Friday showed, per ANI. Foreign currency assets dropped $10.66bn to $604.75bn, while gold reserves declined $2.29bn to $106.41bn. Reserves remain $43.5bn above end-March 2026 levels and $34.6bn higher year-on-year, as the RBI keeps managing rupee volatility.
